findings.comment: Building elevation drawings are not included in the bound plan set. The complete sheet index (39 sheets) contains no building elevation sheets; all architectural elevations are absent from the bound plan set. Elevations must be provided for all proposed buildings.

Elevation sheets are not provided for any of the eight buildings on the site, nor are elevations provided for any required sides of the buildings. Separate architectural elevation drawings must be provided for each building showing all required elevations (typically north, south, east, and west facades).

For developments with multiple distinct building types, separate architectural elevation sheets are not provided for each building type. The site contains three distinct building types (4-Plex, 5-Plex, and 6-Plex); separate elevation sheets must be provided for each building type to demonstrate compliance with architectural standards.

Elevation sheets do not show the average adjacent grade (AAG) calculation identifying the highest and lowest grade points at the building perimeter, nor do they show the vertical dimension from AAG to the applicable measurement point. While Sheet 9 shows "Average (MSL)" values in the Building Height Table, no calculation is provided showing how the AAG was derived from highest and lowest adjacent grades at the building perimeter, and no vertical dimension line on elevation drawings connects AAG to the roof measurement point.

Height measurement method does not match roof type as required by LDC § 25-1-21(50). Without architectural elevation drawings showing the roof type and the applicable measurement point (coping for flat roofs, average height of highest gable for pitched/hip roofs, deck line for mansard roofs, highest point for other styles), the correct measurement method cannot be verified. Elevation sheets must clearly identify the roof type and show the measurement point used to comply with the code-required method.

Rooftop structures above the maximum permitted building height are not labeled on elevation sheets as height limit exceptions. Without architectural elevation drawings, the presence of rooftop structures (parapets, mechanical equipment, chimneys, vents, stairways, elevator penthouses, etc.) and their relationship to the height limit line cannot be verified. Elevation sheets must clearly show and label any rooftop elements that extend above the maximum permitted building height.

Rooftop structure height exceptions cannot be verified without elevation sheets showing the height limit line and any overage calculations. The maximum allowable overage per § 25-2-531 is the greater of: (1) 15% of permitted height; (2) federal/state compliance amount; (3) engineering standard for stacks/vents; or (4) 30% for spires. Elevation sheets must provide a calculation demonstrating that any rooftop extensions remain within the allowable overage, with the calculation shown on the drawing.

For buildings subject to upper-story step-back requirements, the step-back location and dimensions are not shown on elevation sheets with required dimension callouts. The site plan does not document whether step-back requirements apply to these buildings. Elevation sheets must clearly show step-back locations, dimensions, and setback measurements if required by applicable zoning standards.
